summary: Y2O3 thin films were deposited using atomic layer deposition (ALD) with yttrium tris(N,N′-diisopropylacetamidinate) (Y(iPr2amd)3) and water as precursors. The films exhibited a high growth rate of 0.8 Å/cycle, smooth surface morphology, and excellent electrical properties. The process was carried out over a wide temperature range (150-280 °C), and the films showed good thermal stability and low impurity levels.
evidence: Y2O3 thin film was deposited by atomic layer deposition (ALD) with a new precursor yttrium tris(N,N′-diisopropylacetamidinate), Y(iPr2amd)3, and water. The growth rate of Y2O3 films was 0.8 Å/cycle over a wide temperature range (150-280 °C). The films were very pure (C, N < 0.5 at. %) and had a refractive index of 1.8. The films were smooth and had a cubic polycrystalline structure.
